pointers.sentence: It also says why the class is a `TransactionTestCase`: threads do not share transactions, unless they use SQLite's database in memory, and each must commit for the other to see its changes ([Emptying the tables after each test: `TransactionTestCase`](transaction-test-case.md); `django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerTestCase`).

It appends `allowed_host` to `ALLOWED_HOSTS` with `modify_settings`, entered as a context of the class, and starts the server with `LiveServerTestCase._start_server_thread` (`django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerTestCase.setUpClass`, `django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerTestCase._start_server_thread`):

`_terminate_thread` calls `LiveServerThread.terminate`, then `BaseDatabaseWrapper.dec_thread_sharing` on each shared connection (`django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerTestCase._terminate_thread`).

An exception on the way is kept as the thread's error and `is_ready` set, to end the wait; in a `finally` the thread closes its connections (`django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerThread.run`, `django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerThread._create_server`).

An exception on the way is kept as the thread's error and `is_ready` set, to end the wait; in a `finally` the thread closes its connections (`django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerThread.run`, `django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerThread._create_server`).

`ThreadedWSGIServer.process_request_thread` puts the shared connections in place on each such thread, and `ThreadedWSGIServer.close_request` closes the thread's connections when the client's connection ends (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:ThreadedWSGIServer`).
`_make_connections_override` takes those of the test thread's connections that are SQLite's to a database in memory (`django/test/testcases.py:LiveServerTestCase._make_connections_override`).

The server's threads use those very objects, so they see what the test wrote, committed or not, and their closing does not destroy the database: SQLite's `DatabaseWrapper.close` ignores a close of a database in memory (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.close`).
The documentation warns against the two threads querying through it at once: a test should wait for a page to load before going on (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`).

`FSFilesHandler.__call__` hands the application inside every request whose path is not under the URL's path, and all of them when the URL names a host (`django/test/testcases.py:FSFilesHandler._should_handle`).

A missing file, or a directory, raises `Http404`, and the request goes on to `BaseHandler.get_response`: the file handler's own chain, not the application inside, for as a `WSGIHandler` it built the middleware chain when it was made (`django/test/testcases.py:FSFilesHandler.get_response`).

The documentation gives that as the reason for `StaticLiveServerTestCase`, whose `static_handler` is the static files application's `StaticFilesHandler`, serving from the finders ([Serving static files: `StaticFilesHandler` and the development server](../contrib/serving-static.md); `docs/howto/static-files/index.txt`).

An empty `MEDIA_URL`, the default, is read as the script prefix, ordinarily `"/"` (`django/conf/__init__.py:LazySettings._add_script_prefix`), so the media handler takes every path, and with `MEDIA_ROOT` empty too it serves the current directory: /manage.py gets the project's manage.py.
